content: 1. The recommended dosage of atogepant is 10 mg orally once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. 2. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors not contraindicated with darunavir, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 3. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of avanafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may lead to significant adverse events such as severe hypotension, syncope, visual changes, and priapism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use an alternative drug if necessary. 5. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the axitinib dose by 50%. Close monitoring is required. 6. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Close monitoring is required. 8. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate as per its prescribing information. Close monitoring is required. 9. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Close monitoring is required. 10. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of benzphetamine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of betibeglogene autotemcel. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least one month before mobilization or during the elimination period and until all apheresis cycles are completed, as they may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis-derived cells. 12. Darunavir increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, then 40 mg orally daily if co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 14. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bosutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the bosutinib dose by 50%. Close monitoring is required. 17. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients for adverse reactions. 18. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also administered with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. Close monitoring is required. 19. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of brigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor cannot be avoided, reduce the brigatinib dose by approximately 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Close monitoring is required. 20. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 21. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Carefully titrate the dose when initiating buprenorphine, buprenorphine/naloxone, or methadone in patients taking darunavir/cobicistat. Adjust the dose and monitor clinical signs and symptoms when initiating cobicistat in patients taking buprenorphine. Close monitoring is required. 23. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. Implant removal may be necessary if dose adjustment is not feasible. Close monitoring is required. 24. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine transdermal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to the potential for increased toxicity. Close monitoring is required. 28. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cabergoline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Close monitoring is required. 30. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dose of calcifediol as needed and monitor serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations when initiating or discontinuing a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Close monitoring is required. 31. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of calcitriol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 32. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Close monitoring is required. 33. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. Close monitoring is required. 34. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance to darunavir. Close monitoring is required. 36. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Close monitoring is required. 37. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. Close monitoring is required. 39. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ceritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if possible. If unavoidable, reduce the ceritinib dose by approximately 33% and resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Close monitoring is required. 40. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 41. Chloramphenicol increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 42. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose and use alternatives if available. Close monitoring is required. 43. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity, including Cushing's syndrome or adrenal suppression. 44. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of darunavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Close monitoring is required. 46. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Monitor for antidepressant response. 48. Darunavir increases the levels of clarithromycin by inhibiting its metabolism. No dose adjustment is necessary in normal renal function. If creatinine clearance is 30–60 mL/min, reduce the clarithromycin dose by 50%. Close monitoring is required.
